claims.text: A staff note from 2026-07-01 lists levothyroxine 50 mcg each morning in the medication list.
A clinician note from 2026-08-05 documents a plan to increase levothyroxine 75 mcg daily starting Monday because TSH remains high.

citations.quote: Increase levothyroxine 75 mcg daily from Monday

claims.text: The record contains a dose conflict for levothyroxine: 50mcg versus 75mcg.

open_questions: Which levothyroxine dose is currently active: 50 mcg daily or 75 mcg daily?
Was the increase to levothyroxine 75 mcg daily actually started or dispensed after the 2026-08-05 note?
What was the levothyroxine dose and start date at the earliest record, and what doses were documented over time?
What earlier TSH values and trends prompted the dose increase, and what is the most recent TSH result?
Is a thyroid diagnosis or prior dose titration rationale documented in older entries?
Were any follow-up TSH tests or endocrinology referrals planned after the dose change?
Are any allergies or reactions recorded for this patient?

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: Medication list documents levothyroxine 50 mcg each morning, which conflicts with the 75 mcg dose in the later clinician note.
candidate_highlights.suggested_action: Confirm which levothyroxine dose is currently active and reconcile the medication list.

citation.quote: Increase levothyroxine 75 mcg daily from Monday

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: Clinician note directs a levothyroxine dose increase to 75 mcg daily while the medication list still records 50 mcg, and it is unclear whether the change was started or dispensed.
candidate_highlights.suggested_action: Verify whether the 75 mcg daily dose was started or dispensed and update the medication list accordingly.
